https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/n.title: Nigeria tests upgraded biometric voter system ahead of 2027 elections
https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/n.summary: Nigeria’s Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is stress-testing its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and preparing 57,000 additional devices ahead of the 2027 general elections, seeking to prevent a recurrence of the technical failures and controversies that undermined confidence in the 2023 vote.
https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/n.summary_zh: 尼日利亚独立国家选举委员会（INEC）正在对双模式选民登记系统（BVAS）进行压力测试，并为2027年大选准备57,000台额外设备，以防止技术故障和争议再次发生并重蹈2023年投票削弱公众信心的覆辙。
https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/n.body: Nigeria’s Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is stress-testing its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and preparing 57,000 additional devices ahead of the 2027 general elections, seeking to prevent a recurrence of the technical failures and controversies that undermined confidence in the 2023 vote. A six-day nationwide testing exercise was scheduled for October 23–28, followed by a mock accreditation exercise in November. Presidential and National Assembly elections are set for January 16, 2027, with governorship and state legislative elections following on February 6. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan says the upgraded BVAS devices are expected to perform more reliably than those used in previous elections. Introduced in 2021 to replace the earlier smart card reader system, BVAS was first piloted in Delta State before being deployed in several state elections. Its first nationwide use came during Nigeria’s 2023 general elections. According to INEC, BVAS uses fingerprint or facial verification to match voters against the electoral register. The devices also capture images of polling-unit result sheets for upload to the public IReV results portal. During the pilot deployment and in the state governorship elections in 2021 and 2022, concerns about the failure of the devices were rife across many polling stations. The complaints were even louder during the national elections in 2023. But the federal government’s appraisal of the BVAS deployment was largely positive, despite the barrage of criticisms that featured in reports during and after the vote. The then Minister of Information, Lai Mohammed, said that the use of the technology was a game changer as it enabled Nigeria to hold one of the most credible elections in its history. This did not sit well with some civil society organizations. One of them, Yiaga Africa, reported that the BVAS malfunctioned in about 11 percent of polling units during the 2023 presidential election, with nine percent fixed on-site and two percent replaced. Separately, during INEC’s pre-election mock accreditation, Yiaga found that voters were denied accreditation in about 20 percent of polling units because the BVAS could not verify their fingerprints or facial identity. Another report from the EU observer mission indicated that the failures of the BVAS and IReV systems, combined with a lack of transparency, severely damaged public trust in the electoral process. A Commonwealth Observer Group report reached a similar conclusion, stating that BVAS and IReV failures negatively affected the overall credibility and transparency of the polls. INEC says it is aware of the issues and has been taking measures to ready itself for the challenge ahead. According to Amupitan, the new BVAS devices acquired have come with “software hardening, battery optimization, and biometric calibration,” and they also have built-in batteries to address a known weak point in 2023, which was power issues, especially in far-flung and difficult-to-reach communities that do not have electricity connection. On another note, the INEC chair said the body decided to strengthen its existing technology system rather than opting to introduce an untested one, given the limited time it has to get ready for the upcoming elections. One other novelty, according to INEC, is an enhanced e-EC8A system which has been added to the BVAS, and which will be used in digitizing polling unit result sheets, authenticating them cryptographically before uploading them into the IReV portal. This has however stirred controversy as 14 civil society organizations, in August, complained about the system, saying it raises concerns about who actually controls election results once they have been transmitted from the polling stations. INEC, meanwhile, says it has also put in place an AI department, and is working to add an AI-powered anomaly detection system, which will facilitate identifying irregularities in the results transmission process. According to a survey conducted by Yiaga Africa and reported early this month by Punch, only about 49 percent of Nigerians trust BVAS and the IReV systems for voter accreditation and results transmission. The survey showed about 84 percent of Nigerians intend to vote in the upcoming election, but about 61 percent of them say they fear violence, which could arise in the event of technical glitches suffered by BVAS users. Yiaga Africa has urged INEC to commit publicly to real-time uploads of results to the IReV portal, among other concrete reforms. The problem is not Nigeria’s alone. Researchers across the continent have taken note of similar gaps between what biometric systems promise and what they deliver. Dr Henry Mekole, African elections expert and researcher, who has studied Cameroon’s biometric registration system and other African election related issues, told Biometric Update Nigeria must learn from the mistakes of the 2023 elections and take the necessary corrective steps. “The system used by BVAS in 2023 was not only obsolete; it was equally bound to crash. It could not identify and authenticate voters properly; it could not work effectively because of heat and power failure; the network connection was poor, amongst others,” Mekole recalled. “For Nigeria to fix the problem and get the [2027] presidential election right, they need to fix the BVAS system. What should they do? INEC should get the system to be able to properly verify and authenticate voters at polling stations, enhance the network, use solar systems and generators as backups in rural areas, and make it possible to upload the results on time,” he suggested. This concern also resonates with Ghana which is cited among the examples of African countries with maturing use of biometrics in elections . It also suffered biometric verification failures in 2012, partly due to a lack of real-time connectivity and poor staff training. However, things got exceedingly better during the 2024 presidential elections for which 18 million citizens registered to vote. “In Ghana, the biometric process is not only complete; the government equally has the political will to make the system successful. Biometrics in Ghana is used for registration, verification and authentication using high-level technology. For example, the voter’s card, which is issued immediately after registration, has a barcode for verification,” Mekole opined. The Ghana and Nigeria experiences show that maturity in the deployment of biometric systems for election does not come overnight. It requires an assemblage of factors and constant efforts to improve existing systems. Ghana, for example, took three election cycles to be able to normalize its biometric verification system. In Nigeria, the country will be deploying biometric verification only for the second time in a national election. The one important thing many believe will also strengthen the use of the biometric voter verification system in Nigeria is the legal framework. For the first time, the country’s electoral law expressly mentions BVAS as a method of voter accreditation. This is in Section 47(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. For a country like Cameroon which has also had a biometric enrollment system since 2012 , Mekole says the system still has several issues that need to be improved upon, and has not done much to improve election credibility in the Central African nation. The country held a highly disputed presidential election in October last year. “Cameroon opted to use the biometric system to manage its elections in 2013. Between 2013 and 2025, the country was able to acquire more modern kits, improve its capacity to use the kits, and above all, send teams to backward areas to register voters. However, the use of the biometric system has not achieved much in making the country’s elections transparent, fair and credible, for several reasons,” Mekole mentioned. He attributes this, among other reasons, to the delayed issuance of voter cards , the non-use of biometrics for voter identification, and the lack of a central server or network that receives results from different polling stations. Biometrics is not the silver bullet, according to Mekole. But he holds that for the use of the technology to make more sense in African elections, there is need to deploy systems that work beyond just voter enrollment and database deduplication. “Out of 54 African countries, 40 use biometrics for different projects and initiatives. Thirty-five countries use biometrics for election purposes. Most of the election management bodies (EMBs) in Africa use biometric systems more to register voters and to clean up the database. This doesn’t help much to make elections transparent, fair and credible,” Mekole states. “If we truly want to go biometric, then we must use it to register, clean up the database, use it to identify, verify and authenticate voters at different polling stations on voting day, and above all, build a central server or network that can receive and tally results,” he suggested. This of course, he adds, must be backed by strong political will to do things right. “The system cannot on its own expunge underage and other illegal voters. It cannot stop vote buying. It cannot stop the corruption of monitors or other election officials. In Cameroon, for example, it takes 15 days to proclaim the final results for a presidential election. During this period, many funny things would have happened to the results.” “For an election to be fair, transparent and credible, and for all the contestants to accept the results, there must be the political will. This is what we don’t see in many African countries. Biometrics can only do as much.” In all of this, Mekole emphasises the importance of trust and data protection safeguards, which to him, are important in building credibility. He believes deploying the technology alone is not enough. “The biometric system has helped to enhance the integrity of elections in several African countries, but at the same time, it has brought about a lot of risks, breaches of data and privacy. This is so because citizens give out a lot of private and sensitive data during registration,” he said. “To fix this problem, countries must enact strong legal systems that can adequately protect citizens. The laws must protect the biometric data given out by voters. https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/n.title_zh: 尼日利亚在2027年选举前测试升级版生物识别选民系统
https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/n.body_zh: 尼日利亚独立国家选举委员会（INEC）正在对双模式选民登记系统（BVAS）进行压力测试，并为2027年大选准备57000台额外设备，以防止重演削弱公众对2023年投票信心的技术故障和争议。全国性测试计划于10月23日至28日进行，为期6天，随后于11月举行模拟登记演练。总统和国民议会选举定于2027年1月16日举行，州长和州议会选举将于2月6日举行。INEC主席乔阿什·阿穆皮坦表示，升级后的BVAS设备预计将比历届选举使用的设备运行更可靠。BVAS于2021年推出，用于取代早期的智能卡读卡器系统，最初在Delta州试点，随后部署于多个州的选举。该系统首次在全国范围内使用是在尼日利亚2023年大选中。据INEC介绍，BVAS使用指纹或面部核验，将选民与选民登记册进行比对。设备还会拍摄投票站计票结果单的图像，并将其上传至公开的IReV结果门户网站。在试点部署以及2021年和2022年的州长选举期间，许多投票站频繁出现有关设备失灵的担忧。2023年全国选举期间，相关抱怨更加激烈。尽管投票期间及投票后发布的报道中充斥着批评，联邦政府对BVAS部署工作的评价总体上仍较为积极。时任信息部长拉伊·穆罕默德表示，这项技术的使用改变了局面，使尼日利亚得以举行其历史上最可信的选举之一。但这一说法并未得到一些公民社会组织的认可。其中一个组织“亚加非洲”报告称，在2023年总统选举期间，约11%的投票站出现BVAS故障，其中9%在现场得到修复，2%被更换。另据“亚加非洲”在INEC选前模拟登记期间发现，约20%的投票站拒绝为选民登记，因为BVAS无法核验他们的指纹或面部身份。欧盟观察员团的另一份报告指出，BVAS和IReV系统的故障加之透明度不足，严重损害了公众对选举程序的信任。英联邦观察员组的报告也得出了类似结论，称BVAS和IReV故障对投票的总体可信度和透明度产生了负面影响。INEC表示已意识到这些问题，并正在采取措施，为即将面临的挑战做好准备。阿穆皮坦称，新采购的BVAS设备具备“强化软件、优化电池和生物识别校准”等功能，还配有内置电池，以解决2023年选举中一个已知薄弱环节，即供电问题，尤其是在没有电网连接、偏远且难以抵达的社区。INEC主席还表示，鉴于准备即将到来的选举时间有限，该机构决定强化现有技术系统，而不是引入未经测试的新系统。据INEC介绍，另一项新功能是升级版e-EC8A系统，该系统已并入BVAS，用于将投票站计票结果单数字化，并在上传至IReV门户网站之前以加密方式进行真实性验证。不过，此举引发了争议。今年8月，14个公民社会组织对该系统提出质疑，称结果从投票站传送后由谁实际掌控，会引发对选举结果控制权的担忧。与此同时，INEC表示还设立了人工智能部门，并正着手增加一套由人工智能驱动的异常检测系统，以帮助识别结果传输过程中的违规异常。据“亚加非洲”开展的一项调查以及《Punch》本月早些时候的报道，只有约49%的尼日利亚人信任BVAS和IReV系统能够完成选民登记及结果传输。调查显示，约84%的尼日利亚人打算在即将到来的选举中投票，但其中约61%担心发生暴力事件；这类暴力可能因BVAS用户遭遇技术故障而引发。“亚加非洲”敦促INEC公开承诺实时将结果上传至IReV门户网站，并落实其他具体改革。问题并非尼日利亚独有。全非洲的研究人员已经注意到生物识别系统的承诺与其实际表现之间存在类似差距。研究喀麦隆生物识别登记系统及其他非洲选举相关问题的非洲选举专家和研究员亨利·梅科勒博士告诉《Biometric Update》，尼日利亚必须从2023年选举的错误中吸取教训，并采取必要的纠正措施。梅科勒回顾道：“BVAS在2023年使用的系统不仅已经过时，而且同样注定会崩溃。它无法正确识别和认证选民；由于高温和停电等因素，无法有效运行；网络连接也很差，此外还存在其他问题。”“若尼日利亚要解决问题并办好[2027年]总统选举，就需要修复BVAS系统。他们应该怎么做？INEC应让该系统能够在投票站正确核验和认证选民，改善网络状况，在农村地区使用太阳能系统和发电机作为备用电源，并确保能够及时上传结果。”他建议道。这一担忧在加纳同样存在。加纳被列为非洲逐步成熟运用生物识别技术进行选举的国家之一。2012年，加纳也遭遇过生物识别核验故障，部分原因是缺乏实时连接以及工作人员培训不足。然而，2024年总统选举期间，情况已大为改善，共有1800万公民登记投票。梅科勒认为：“在加纳，生物识别程序不仅已经完善，政府也具备让该系统成功运行的政治意愿。加纳利用先进技术进行选民登记、核验和认证。例如，登记后立即发放的选民证带有用于核验的条形码。”加纳和尼日利亚的经验表明，成熟部署用于选举的生物识别系统并非一蹴而就。它需要多种因素相互配合，并持续努力改进现有系统。以加纳为例，该国用了3个选举周期才使生物识别核验系统实现常态化。在尼日利亚，该国仅是第二次在全国选举中部署生物识别核验。许多人认为，还有一项重要因素能够加强尼日利亚生物识别选民核验系统的使用，那就是法律框架。该国选举法首次明确将BVAS列为选民登记方法，具体规定见《2026年选举法》第47(2)条。对于喀麦隆这样自2012年起也采用生物识别登记系统的国家，梅科勒表示，该系统仍存在若干有待改进的问题，在提升这个中非国家选举可信度方面成效甚微。去年10月，该国举行了一场争议极大的总统选举。梅科勒提到：“喀麦隆于2013年决定采用生物识别系统管理选举。2013年至2025年间，该国得以购置更先进的设备，提高使用这些设备的能力，最重要的是派遣工作队前往欠发达地区登记选民。然而，出于若干原因，生物识别系统的使用并未在很大程度上推动该国选举实现透明、公平和可信。”他认为，原因包括选民证发放延迟、未使用生物识别技术识别选民，以及缺少接收不同投票站结果的中央服务器或网络。在梅科勒看来，生物识别技术并非万能良方。但他认为，要让这项技术在非洲选举中发挥更大意义，就需要部署超越选民登记和数据库去重等基础用途的系统。梅科勒表示：“在非洲54个国家中，有40个国家将生物识别技术用于不同项目和倡议，其中35个国家将其用于选举。非洲大多数选举管理机构（EMB）使用生物识别系统，主要是为了登记选民和清理数据库。这对推动选举透明、公平和可信帮助不大。”“如果我们真正要走向生物识别，就必须利用它登记选民、清理数据库，在投票日用不同投票站识别、核验和认证选民，最重要的是建立能够接收并汇总结果的中央服务器或网络。”他建议道。当然，他补充说，做好这些事情还必须得到强有力的政治意愿支持。“该系统无法自行清除未成年选民和其他非法选民，无法制止买票，也无法阻止选监人员或其他选举官员腐败。例如，在喀麦隆，总统选举公布最终结果需要15天。在这段时间里，结果可能已经发生各种匪夷所思的变故。”他指出：“要使选举公平、透明、可信，并让所有参选者接受结果，就必须具备政治意愿。这是我们在许多非洲国家都看不到的。生物识别技术能发挥的作用有限。”在所有这些问题中，梅科勒强调信任和数据保护保障措施的重要性。在他看来，这些是建立可信度的关键。单靠部署技术并不足够。他说：“生物识别系统帮助若干非洲国家提高了选举的Integrity，但与此同时，也带来了诸多风险、数据泄露和隐私侵犯。这是因为公民在登记期间会提供大量私密和敏感数据。”“要解决这一问题，各国必须制定强有力的法律制度，充分保护公民。法律必须保护选民提供的生物识别数据。数据不应移交给第三方，而且公众必须始终了解选举管理机构如何处理他们提交的数据。”澳大利亚正敦促美国接受一种身份验证模式，该模式可让美国边境当局对旅客进行筛查……本网站使用Akismet减少垃圾评论。了解评论数据的处理方式

https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mum.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) will undertake a nine-day special cleanliness and dust mitigation drive across Mumbai from October 29 to November 6, focusing on major arterial roads and dust-prone stretches to curb air pollution and improve the city’s air quality ahead of Diwali. The drive, initiated on the directions of Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide, will cover major roads, including the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR), Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR), Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) Connector, Eastern Express Highway and Western Express Highway. Other identified stretches include Ghatkopar-Mankhurd Road, Sion-Mankhurd Road, S.V. Road, Link Road and Carter Road. According to instructions issued by the civic body’s Solid Waste Management (SWM) Department, the exercise will involve intensive road sweeping, removal of accumulated dust, silt and construction and demolition (C&D) waste, and cleaning of road dividers, medians, traffic islands, footpaths and kerbs. Water sprinkling and misting will also be carried out at identified dust-prone locations. The BMC has allocated ₹15 lakh to each municipal ward for the drive. Assistant Engineers from the SWM Department have been instructed to prepare day-wise action plans in coordination with their respective ward Assistant Commissioners, identifying locations requiring intensive cleaning and the manpower and machinery needed. The civic body will deploy mechanical sweepers, misting machines, water sprinklers, JCBs, dumpers and litter pickers, using both departmental and contractual resources. Officials have also been instructed to ensure that sanitation workers are provided with uniforms, protective gear and necessary safety equipment. Assistant Commissioners and zonal Deputy Municipal Commissioners have been asked to personally oversee the exercise to ensure effective implementation and visible improvements on the ground. Zonal SWM officials will also assess requirements for additional machinery and manpower and coordinate their deployment wherever necessary. To monitor the drive, each ward will be required to maintain daily records of locations covered, activities undertaken, manpower and machinery deployed, and quantities of dust and waste collected and disposed of. The reporting process will also include geo-tagged photographs and videos documenting conditions before and after the cleaning operations. The SWM Department’s operations team will centrally compile progress reports, while the civic body’s public relations department has been instructed to periodically share verified updates with the media and keep citizens informed about the drive’s progress and outcomes. The initiative is part of the BMC’s precautionary measures to control road dust and maintain Mumbai’s Air Quality Index (AQI) during the winter season, when deteriorating air quality remains a concern. Road、Link Road 和 Carter Road。根据该市政机构固体废物管理（SWM）部门发布的指令，此次行动将包括加强道路清扫，清除积尘、淤泥以及建筑和拆除（C&D）废弃物，并清洁道路隔离带、中央分隔带、交通岛、人行道和路缘。还将对确定的易扬尘地点洒水和喷雾。BMC 已为每个市政区划拨15万卢比，用于开展此次行动。SWM 部门的助理工程师已获指示，须与各自所在区划的助理市政专员协调，制定每日行动计划，确定需要重点清洁的地点以及所需人力和机械。市政机构将调配道路清扫车、喷雾机、洒水车、JCB、自卸货车和垃圾捡拾车，并使用部门自有及承包资源。官员还获指示，须确保为环卫工人配发制服、防护装备和必要的安全设备。助理市政专员和分区副市政专员已被要求亲自监督行动，确保有效落实并让当地环境取得明显改善。分区 SWM 官员还将评估对额外机械和人力的需求，并在必要时协调调配。为监测此次行动，每个区划均须每日记录已覆盖地点、已开展活动、已调配人力和机械，以及收集并处置的扬尘和废弃物数量。报告流程还将包括带地理标记的照片和视频，记录清洁作业前后的状况。SWM 部门行动团队将集中汇总进度报告，该市政机构公共关系部门则获指示，须定期向媒体发布经核实的信息，并向市民通报行动进展和成果。该举措是 BMC 在冬季空气质量持续恶化、污染问题仍令人担忧之际，为控制道路扬尘并维持孟买空气质量指数（AQI）而采取的预防措施之一。评论必须使用英语，并以完整句子表述。评论不得含有辱骂性内容或针对个人的攻击。请遵守我们的社区准则后再发表评论。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果您已是《The Hindu》注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们文章的讨论。如果您没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以查看以往在 Vuukle 上发表的评论

https://www.myjoyonline.com/underage-gir.body: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of 34-year-old mobile money vendor Christian Amponsah, whose body was discovered at a guest house around Kasoa Second in the Central Region. The Central East Regional Police Command said the suspects, identified as 59-year-old Felicia Osei Appiah, 24-year-old Clement Opoku Yeboah and a female juvenile, were arrested on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. According to the police, the arrests followed investigations into the death of Amponsah after the manager of the guest house reported discovering the victim lying motionless in a room. The manager told police that the deceased and the juvenile had checked into the guest house and booked a room for two hours. When the booking period elapsed and neither occupant emerged, he went to check on them. He reportedly discovered Amponsah lying motionless in a pool of blood, prompting a report to the police. Officers who visited the scene found the deceased lying face down, with bedsheets, curtains and pillows covering his body. The body was subsequently conveyed to the Police Hospital Mortuary in Accra for preservation, identification and autopsy. The three suspects are currently in police custody and assisting with investigations as authorities work to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing and the respective roles, if any, of those arrested. The Command said investigations were ongoing and that steps were being taken to put the suspects before court

https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.summary: The bill is the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted by the National Assembly to the 36 state Houses of Assembly for concurrence. Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it seeks to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police.
https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.summary_zh: 该法案是《尼日利亚联邦共和国宪法（第六次修订）法案（2026年）》，由国民议会提交给36个州议会审议并表示同意。在提交法案时，Abdullahi表示，该法案旨在修订1999年宪法，以建立各州警察机构，同时保留尼日利亚警察部队作为联邦警察机构。
https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.body: The bill was passed on Tuesday evening during plenary presided over by the Speaker, Alhaji Tukur Bala Bodinga. Bodinga, who confirmed the development to LEADERSHIP, said the House would soon issue an official statement on its decision. “Yes, we have passed the bill yesterday. You will see the statement any moment from now,” he said. The bill is the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted by the National Assembly to the 36 state Houses of Assembly for concurrence. The motion was moved by the Deputy Majority Leader, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC – Sokoto South II). Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it seeks to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police. He said the bill was transmitted by the executive, considered by the Senate on June 24 and the House of Representatives on July 23, and presented to the Sokoto Assembly on September 22. Abdullahi explained that under the proposed framework, the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory and protection of federal assets. He said state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property and investigation of local crimes. He added that the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police, to be appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly. He said a State Police Service Commission would be responsible for appointment, promotion and discipline of personnel and would receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy. The passage brings the number of state assemblies that have endorsed the bill to 28, exceeding the constitutional requirement of 24 states, or two-thirds of the 36 assemblies, needed for alteration of the Constitution. The development comes amid persistent security challenges in Sokoto and the North-West, where banditry, kidnapping and attacks on rural communities have disrupted farming and livelihoods. Proponents argue that officers recruited from local communities would better understand the terrain and improve intelligence gathering. https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.title_zh: 州警察法案：索科托州议会加入另外27个议会行列
https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.body_zh: 该法案于周二晚间在众议院议长Alhaji Tukur Bala Bodinga主持的全会上获得通过。Bodinga向《LEADERSHIP》证实了这一进展，并表示众议院很快将就其决定发布正式声明。他说：“是的，我们昨天通过了该法案。你们很快就会看到声明。”该法案是《1999年尼日利亚联邦共和国宪法（第六次修订）法案（2026年）》，由国民议会提交给36个州议会审议并取得一致同意。动议由多数党副领袖Mustapha Abdullahi（APC–索科托南二选区）提出。Abdullahi在提交法案时表示，该法案旨在修订1999年宪法，以建立各州警察机构，同时保留尼日利亚警察部队作为联邦警察。他说，该法案由行政部门提交，参议院于6月24日审议，众议院于7月23日审议，并于9月22日提交索科托州议会。Abdullahi解释称，根据拟议框架，联邦警察将负责处理跨州和国际犯罪、恐怖主义、网络犯罪、边境安全、联邦首都辖区治安以及联邦资产保护。他说，各州警察机构将负责执法、维护公共秩序与安全、保护生命和财产，以及调查地方犯罪。他补充说，各州警察机构的负责人将称为警察州指挥官，由州长根据国家警察委员会的建议任命，并须经州议会确认。他说，州警察服务委员会将负责人员的任命、晋升和纪律管理，并直接从州综合收入基金获得资金，以确保财政自主。该法案获通过后，已有28个州议会表示支持，超过修改宪法所需的24个州、即36个州议会中三分之二的要求。索科托州及西北部持续面临安全挑战，土匪活动、绑架和对农村社区的袭击已扰乱农业生产和生计。支持者认为，从当地社区招募的警员能够更好地了解地形，并改善情报收集工作。据报道，周二最新获得批准的是卡诺、索科托、埃博尼和拉各斯州。欢迎关注我们的优势服务。实时报道、突发独家消息和独家视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入《LEADERSHIP NEWS》的WhatsApp频道，获取全天候最新动态 →

https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghana-signs-.body: Ghana has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Russia’s Republic of Tatarstan to facilitate employment opportunities for Ghanaian citizens under the Alabuga Start programme. The agreement was signed between the Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment and the Alabuga Special Economic Zone, with the aim of strengthening cooperation in the employment of Ghanaian citizens. Among the officials present at the signing were E.R. Safiullin, Acting Director of Alabuga; Senator Muhametshin; Gatin, an adviser to the Rais of Tatarstan; and Ahmetshin, Permanent Representative of Tatarstan to Moscow. Speaking after the signing in Russia, Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment, Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum, said the agreement would open up opportunities for Ghana’s youthful population to access jobs with competitive salaries, accommodation and residence permits. He said the government was committed to ensuring that Ghanaians recruited under the arrangement received appropriate employment opportunities and adequate protection. “We’re going to make sure that they get the right jobs to do, they are protected, they are being given the right conditions of service,” he said. Kwadwo Agyekum explained that the agreement extends beyond labour migration, with both parties exploring opportunities for business collaboration, academic research, and cultural and religious exchanges. He said Ghanaian businesses were expected to participate in upcoming business forums, while universities and academic institutions would be encouraged to collaborate on research initiatives. The Minister added that the government would continue pursuing international partnerships aimed at expanding employment opportunities for young people

https://punchng.com/tinubus-reforms-boos.title: Tinubu’s reforms boost sugar self-sufficiency drive
https://punchng.com/tinubus-reforms-boos.summary: The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the National Sugar Development Council, Kamar Bakrin, has said the macroeconomic reforms introduced by President Bola Tinubu have made local sugar production attractive and cleared the path for Nigeria to achieve self-sufficiency in sugar. Under the Nigeria Sugar Master Plan 2.0, the goal is self-sufficiency in sugar production. The Nigeria Sugar Master Plan 2.0 is the country’s strategy for achieving self-sufficiency in sugar production.
https://punchng.com/tinubus-reforms-boos.summary_zh: 国家糖业发展委员会执行秘书兼首席执行官Kamar Bakrin表示，总统Bola Tinubu推出的宏观经济改革提高了本地食糖生产的吸引力，为尼日利亚实现食糖自给自足铺平了道路。根据《尼日利亚糖业总体规划2.0》，目标是实现食糖生产自给自足。《尼日利亚糖业总体规划2.0》是该国实现食糖生产自给自足的战略。
https://punchng.com/tinubus-reforms-boos.body: The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the National Sugar Development Council, Kamar Bakrin, has said the macroeconomic reforms introduced by President Bola Tinubu have made local sugar production attractive and cleared the path for Nigeria to achieve self-sufficiency in sugar. According to a statement on Wednesday, Bakrin stated this when he appeared as a panellist at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NESG #32), during a session on “Strengthening Policy Coordination for the Non-alcoholic Drink Sector Competitiveness.” He said the reforms had brought stability to the economy, adding that the next step was to turn that stability into growth that works for ordinary Nigerians. “Our most pressing priorities are well known: jobs, especially for young people; rural livelihoods; security, pressure on foreign exchange; food security; and the cost of living,” he said. According to him, the council’s role is to ensure that the full economic picture of the sugar value chain is considered whenever the government makes policy choices. “Every Government must make choices among competing priorities. Our contribution as a Council is to make sure that, when those choices are made, the full economic picture of the sugar value chain is on the table. This is because very few sectors touch all of these priorities at once the way sugar does,” the NSDC boss said. Bakrin urged participants to view sugar and beverages as a single value chain, “from the cane field to the bottle.” He noted that the beverage industry is the largest industrial consumer of sugar in Nigeria, meaning that what strengthens one sector strengthens the other. Responding to the summit’s theme, he said sugar offers a practical route to inclusive growth. Under the Nigeria Sugar Master Plan 2.0, the goal is self-sufficiency in sugar production. He said achieving it would save about US$1 billion in foreign exchange annually and create about 110,000 direct jobs, mostly in rural communities, on estates, in mills and on outgrower farms where smallholders grow cane for the mills. “The gains go beyond the factory gate. Sugar estates bring roads, schools, clinics and electricity generated from bagasse, the fibre left after cane is crushed. Sugarcane is also a source of fuel ethanol, bio-electricity and biodegradable packaging, which links to the circular-economy agenda this session is discussing,” he said. He added that investors were already responding to the opportunities in the sector. “Brownfield investors have committed to delivering 1.22 million metric tonnes a year by 2030, two years ahead of the NSMP’s 2032 timeline. A pipeline of greenfield projects is set to add 830,000 metric tonnes a year by 2030,” he said. He added that investor confidence remained very high but could only be sustained through consistent policies. “A sugar estate takes at least four years from land clearing to full production, with capital committed long before the first tonne is sold. Investors therefore look for stable demand and a predictable policy environment,” he told the audience. He stressed that the council fully shares the government’s objectives, including the public-health goal of tackling non-communicable diseases. “We are not asking anyone to choose between health and industry,” he said. He explained that investors weigh two key questions before committing funds: whether there will be stable demand for the sugar, and whether the policy environment will stay predictable throughout the life of the investment. “An investor making that decision looks at two things: will there be stable demand for this sugar, and will the policy environment be predictable over the life of the investment? So, every fiscal and regulatory decision that touches this value chain also sends a signal to the investors we are working hard to attract,” Bakrin added. He proposed that any measure affecting the sugar and beverage value chain should first be assessed for its impact on jobs, investment and the NSMP before being finalised and then introduced with a reasonable transition period through established mechanisms. Bakrin said coherence between government and industry was critical, adding that beverage manufacturers could anchor demand for Nigerian-grown sugar through local offtake commitments, support for outgrower farmers, market data and investment in the Backward Integration Program. “When Government protects the conditions for demand, and industry commits to local supply, the whole value chain grows, and the jobs stay in Nigeria,” he said. He also recommended that the Nigeria Industrial Policy Sectoral Competitiveness and Growth Initiative (NSCGI) adopt alignment with the Sugar Master Plan as one of its measures of success. “When the sugar sector and the beverage sector grow together, Nigeria wins: on jobs, on foreign exchange, and on rural prosperity,” he added. The Nigeria Sugar Master Plan 2.0 is the country’s strategy for achieving self-sufficiency in sugar production. Its delivery is projected to save about US$1 billion in foreign exchange annually and create about 110,000 direct jobs, largely in rural communities. Brownfield investors have committed to delivering 1.22 million metric tonnes a year by 2030, two years ahead of the 2032 timeline, while greenfield projects are expected to add a further 830,000 metric tonnes a year by 2030. https://punchng.com/tinubus-reforms-boos.title_zh: 蒂努布的改革推动糖业实现自给自足
https://punchng.com/tinubus-reforms-boos.body_zh: 国家糖业发展委员会执行秘书兼首席执行官Kamar Bakrin表示，总统Bola Tinubu推出的宏观经济改革提高了本地糖业生产的吸引力，并为尼日利亚实现糖类自给自足铺平了道路。Bakrin周三在一份声明中表示，他作为嘉宾出席第32届尼日利亚经济峰会（NESG #32）期间举行的“加强政策协调以提升无酒精饮料行业竞争力”分会时发表了上述言论。他说，这些改革为经济带来了稳定，并补充称，下一步是把这种稳定转化为惠及普通尼日利亚人的增长。他说：“我们最紧迫的优先事项众所周知：就业，尤其是青年就业；农村生计；安全；外汇压力；粮食安全；以及生活成本。”据他介绍，该委员会的职责是确保政府每次制定政策时，都能全面考虑糖业价值链的经济影响。Bakrin说：“每届政府都必须在相互竞争的优先事项之间作出选择。我们委员会的作用是确保在作出这些选择时，糖业价值链的整体经济影响能够被纳入考量。这是因为，能够像糖业一样同时牵动所有这些优先事项的行业极少。”这位国家糖业发展委员会负责人敦促与会者将糖业和饮料业视为一个完整的价值链，“从甘蔗田到瓶装产品”。他指出，饮料行业是尼日利亚最大的工业用糖户，这意味着强化其中任何一个行业都会带动另一个行业。回应峰会主题时，他说，糖业为包容性增长提供了一条切实可行的道路。根据《尼日利亚糖业总体规划2.0》，目标是实现糖类生产自给自足。他说，实现这一目标每年可节省约US$1 billion外汇，并创造约110,000个直接就业岗位，其中大部分位于农村社区、糖厂以及由小农户为糖厂种植甘蔗的合同种植农场。他说：“这些收益超出了工厂大门的范围。糖业种植园会带来道路、学校、诊所，以及利用甘蔗压榨后留下的纤维——袋渣——发电。甘蔗还是燃料乙醇、生物电力和可降解包装的原料，而后者与本次分会讨论的循环经济议程相契合。”他还表示，投资者已经在响应该行业的机遇。他说：“棕地投资者已承诺到2030年实现每年1.22 million公吨的产量，比NSMP的2032年时间表提前两年。另有多个新建项目管线的产能预计到2030年将增加每年830,000公吨。”他补充说，投资者信心仍然很高，但只有通过持续稳定的政策才能维持这种信心。他对与会者说：“从清理土地到全面投产，一座糖业种植园至少需要四年，而资本早在出售第一批糖之前就已投入。因此，投资者会关注稳定的需求和可预测的政策环境。”他强调，该委员会完全赞同政府的各项目标，包括应对非传染性疾病的公共卫生目标。他说：“我们并未要求任何人在健康与工业之间作出取舍。”他解释道，投资者在投入资金前会权衡两个关键问题：糖类需求是否稳定，以及政策环境能否在整个投资周期内保持可预测。Bakrin补充说：“投资者在作出这一决定时会考量两件事：这种糖的需求是否稳定，以及政策环境在投资周期内是否具有可预测性。因此，每一项涉及这一价值链的财政和监管决定，也是在向我们努力吸引的投资者传递信号。”他提议，任何影响糖业和饮料业价值链的措施，在最终确定并通过既有机制出台之前，都应先评估其对就业、投资和NSMP的影响，并设定合理的过渡期。Bakrin表示，政府与产业之间保持协调至关重要，饮料制造商可以通过承诺采购本地糖、支持合同种植农户、提供市场数据以及投资后向一体化计划，为尼日利亚本地种植的糖类奠定需求基础。他说：“当政府保护需求条件，而产业承诺本地供应时，整个价值链都会增长，就业也会留在尼日利亚。”他还建议，将与《糖业总体规划》协调一致列为尼日利亚产业政策部门竞争力与增长倡议（NSCGI）的成功措施之一。他补充说：“当糖业和饮料业共同发展时，尼日利亚将在就业、外汇和农村繁荣方面成为赢家。”《尼日利亚糖业总体规划2.0》是该国实现糖类生产自给自足的战略。实施该计划预计每年可节省约US$1 billion外汇，并创造约110,000个直接就业岗位，其中大部分位于农村社区。棕地投资者已承诺到2030年实现每年1.22 million公吨的产量，比2032年时间表提前两年，而新建项目预计到2030年将再增加每年830,000公吨。联邦政府支付了GenCos所欠N3.3tn债务中的N1.23tn——Tinubu部长将在年底前提交2027年预算——部长称有关向美国出售$700bn矿产的报道不实，联邦政府表示Adetutu Sobowale Adetutu拥有三年发布有关性别、健康、教育、都市新闻和事实核查报道的经验

https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/10/2.summary_zh: 俄罗斯南部克拉斯诺达尔地方当局因多个垃圾填埋场接近满载而宣布进入高度警戒状态。几年前，克里姆林宫支持的垃圾管理改革本应带来新的处理设施。有关部门表示，在垃圾填埋场重建完成、取得必要许可并建成新的市政垃圾处理设施之前，高度警戒状态将一直维持。
https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/10/2.body: Authorities in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region have declared a high alert over nearly full landfills, years after a Kremlin-backed waste management overhaul was supposed to deliver new processing facilities. Governor Veniamin Kondratyev introduced the measures on Oct. 22 in 10 districts, including the Black Sea resort city of Sochi and the port of Novorossiysk, the regional emergency task force said . It cited the “exhaustion of capacity at waste management facilities.” The governor’s decree warned of a potential regional emergency, with disruptions to garbage collection threatening to leave waste piling up in towns and villages. It also warned of illegal dumping and the spread of infectious diseases carried by rodents and insects, the local news outlet Gorod Krasnodar reported . The decree was published five days after Kondratyev signed it. Authorities said the high alert would remain in place until landfill reconstruction is completed, the necessary permits are secured and new municipal waste processing facilities are built. Ten such facilities are currently under construction, according to the task force. Officials pledged that garbage would continue to be collected regularly along existing routes. Kondratyev put his deputy, Yevgeny Pergun, in charge of addressing the threat. Pergun is also overseeing efforts to resolve the region’s fuel crisis and contain gasoline prices. He was instructed to draw up a plan for building and upgrading waste treatment and disposal facilities and using existing sites. Kondratyev also urged regional waste operators to keep their landfills running until the threat of an emergency has passed. The Krasnodar region, which consistently ranks among Russia’s 10 largest regional economies, was supposed to receive at least eight municipal waste processing complexes under the nationwide waste management reform launched by President Vladimir Putin in 2019. Regional prosecutors had already flagged serious problems in 2024, Gorod Krasnodar reported. Nine of the region’s 15 municipal waste disposal facilities were full, while coastal districts were left without legally operating landfills, prosecutors said. They also found that violations in the selection of construction sites made some planned facilities unusable. None of the nine facilities envisaged under the reform, including eight waste processing complexes, had opened by 2026. Authorities have since pushed back construction deadlines to 2027–2028. The region has allocated 36.8 billion rubles ($456.3 million) to its waste management program through 2030, according to the Kommersant newspaper. https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/10/2.body_zh: 俄罗斯南部克拉斯诺达尔州 authorities 因垃圾填埋场接近满载宣布进入高度警戒状态，而多年前克里姆林宫支持的废物管理改革本应带来新的处理设施。州长韦尼阿明·孔德拉季耶夫于10月22日在包括黑海度假城市索契和港口新罗西斯克在内的10个区采取上述措施。州应急特遣队称，此举是因为“废物处理设施的处理能力已接近耗尽”。据当地新闻 outlet《Gorod Krasnodar》报道，孔德拉季耶夫州长发布的法令警告可能发生区域性紧急状况，垃圾收集中断将威胁城镇和村庄，导致废弃物堆积。法令还警告非法倾倒以及由啮齿动物和昆虫传播的传染病扩散。该法令在孔德拉季耶夫签署5天后公布。当局表示，在填埋场重建完成、取得必要许可证并建成新的市政废物处理设施之前，高度警戒状态将持续有效。据特遣队称，目前有10座此类设施正在施工。官员承诺，垃圾将继续按照现有路线定期收运。孔德拉季耶夫指派其副手叶夫根尼·佩尔贡负责应对这一威胁。佩尔贡还负责解决该地区的燃料危机和控制汽油价格。他奉命制定一项计划，用于建设和升级废物处理及处置设施，并利用现有场址。孔德拉季耶夫还敦促地区废物运营机构维持填埋场运行，直至紧急状况的威胁结束。克拉斯诺达尔州的经济规模始终位居俄罗斯10个最大地区经济之列；根据总统弗拉基米尔·普京于2019年启动的全国废物管理改革，该州原计划至少获得8座市政废物处理综合体。据《Gorod Krasnodar》报道，地区检察官早在2024年就指出存在严重问题。检察官称，该地区15座市政废物处置设施中有9座已经填满，而沿海各区没有合法运营的填埋场。他们还发现，场址选择中的违规行为导致部分规划设施无法使用。截至2026年，改革规划的9座设施，包括8座废物处理综合体，均未投入使用。此后，当局将建设期限推迟至2027年至2028年。据《Kommersant》报纸报道，该州已为截至2030年的废物管理计划拨款368亿卢布（4.563亿美元）。本文借助人工智能完成翻译，并由《The Moscow Times》编辑审阅后发布。可在此进一步了解本编辑部的 AI 政策。阅读本文的俄文版，请访问《The Moscow Times》俄文服务。我们正面临前所未有的挑战。俄罗斯总检察长办公室已将《The Moscow Times》认定为“不受欢迎”组织，将我们的工作刑事化，并使我们的员工面临被起诉的风险。此前，我们还被不公正地贴上“外国代理人”标签。这些行动是企图在俄罗斯压制独立新闻工作的直接举措。当局声称我们的工作“诋毁俄罗斯领导层的决策”。我们持不同看法：我们致力于提供准确、不偏不倚的俄罗斯报道。我们《The Moscow Times》的记者拒绝被噤声。但要继续我们的工作，我们需要您的帮助。您的支持无论多少，都能带来巨大的不同。如果条件允许，请从每月2美元开始支持我们。设置起来很简单，每一笔捐款都会产生显著影响。支持《The Moscow Times》，就是在面对压制时捍卫开放、独立的新闻事业。感谢您与我们同行

https://dailytrust.com/well-rig-those-wh.body: Peter Obi, Presidential Candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), has vowed to take on those who manipulate elections, declaring that his camp will “rig those who rig” the 2027 polls. Obi made the declaration on Wednesday at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State, where he outlined his plans to tackle electoral malpractice and ensure accountability if elected president. “Let me assure you, number one, this coming election, we will rig those who rig it,” he said. The former Anambra State governor said his administration would enforce the rule of law without discrimination, stressing that no individual would be above the law, regardless of position or status. “Under my watch, Nigeria must be a country that has a law and votes from number one person to the last person must obey the rule of law. Nobody will be above the law. Nobody will behave rascally,” he said. Obi also pledged to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system to prevent manipulation and ensure that anyone who interfered with the electoral process faced the consequences. “And let me assure you, number two, if elected the president of Nigeria, nobody will rig the election in this country again,” he said. He warned that political officeholders and electoral officials who manipulated election results under his administration would face prosecution and imprisonment. “Any high-ranking official, anybody who is involved with the election, under my watch, that rigs the election, will go to jail,” Obi said. The NDC presidential candidate also called for stricter enforcement of educational requirements for candidates seeking elective offices, insisting that aspirants must have attended both primary and secondary school. “For you to contest the election, you must have attended a primary school, you must have attended a secondary school, and it will be visible, it will be clear,” he said. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.title: Alake denies $700bn minerals sale, inaugurates Nigeria-US committee
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.summary: ABUJA — Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, has dismissed reports that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States, insisting that no national asset has been sold or transferred under the bilateral cooperation framework.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.summary_zh: 阿布贾——固体矿产发展部长Dele Alake博士否认了有关尼日利亚向美国出售价值$700 billion固体矿产的报道，坚持称在双边合作框架下没有出售或转让任何国有资产。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.body: ABUJA — Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, has dismissed reports that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States, insisting that no national asset has been sold or transferred under the bilateral cooperation framework. Alake spoke on Tuesday in Abuja while inaugurating the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector, describing the reports as false and clarifying that the agreement was designed to attract investment and promote partnerships between American investors and Nigerian operators. “There is no sale of any Nigerian asset. There’s nothing exchanging hands,” he said. The minister explained that the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by Nigeria and the US was a government-to-government platform intended to facilitate business-to-business engagements, rather than transfer ownership of Nigeria’s mineral resources to foreign interests. “We created a platform to facilitate mingling of US investment ventures with Nigeria’s local operators. It is in the public domain. We signed it in public and published it in four or five national newspapers,” he said. The committee’s inauguration followed the strategic cooperation framework established between both countries during the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. Alake also dismissed claims that the United States intended to take over Nigeria’s mineral resources and security architecture, describing the reports as misleading. He said the partnership aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s economic diversification agenda, which seeks to reduce the country’s dependence on crude oil through the sustainable development of its mineral resources. According to him, Nigeria is seeking to change the pattern of international economic transactions in which resource-rich African countries export raw materials without retaining sufficient value from their exploitation. “We have the resources, the critical elements the world needs to transit to clean energy. So we are creating a new paradigm — you bring your capital, expertise and technology, to match with our natural resources and create a win-win situation. The investor gains, Nigeria gains,” he said. The minister lamented that Nigeria had historically operated a mono-product economy, while much of its solid minerals sector remained informal, with ores transported “from pit to port” without adequate local processing. He said the Federal Government had introduced a policy making local processing a condition for the granting of mineral titles, adding that investors must demonstrate a clear pathway for processing minerals within the country. According to Alake, the policy has encouraged the establishment of processing facilities across the country, including what he described as West Africa’s largest lithium processing plant, recently commissioned in Nasarawa State by the Vice President. He said the government’s reform efforts also informed the establishment of the African Minerals Strategy Group, which aims to strengthen cooperation among African countries on mineral development. Alake attributed renewed investor confidence to the macroeconomic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, which he said provided assurances on security of tenure and the repatriation of profits. Charging members of the newly inaugurated committee to discharge their responsibilities diligently, the minister described their assignment as critical to achieving the President’s $1 trillion economy target. He urged the committee to coordinate activities, identify viable investment opportunities and translate the Nigeria-US cooperation framework into measurable outcomes that would strengthen the country’s position in the global solid minerals industry. In his welcome address, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, Engr Faruk Yusuf Yabo, said the inauguration would translate growing bilateral engagements into a structured framework for practical cooperation and investment mobilisation. Also speaking, Economic Officer at the US Embassy, Jonathan Baas, said US President Donald Trump had prioritised three areas for American embassies: energy, artificial intelligence and superintelligence, as well as critical minerals. Baas said Washington was seeking partnerships that would secure critical mineral supply chains while ensuring that partner countries benefited from the value generated. “We just signed a contract today on looking into building AI data centres in Nigeria at the Nigerian Economic Summit. That’s the direction Washington wants us to go,” he said. In his vote of thanks, the Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of the Nigeria Solid Minerals Company (NSMC) said the committee would coordinate implementation, facilitate investment and monitor progress towards achieving the objectives of the Nigeria-US cooperation framework. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.title_zh: 阿拉基否认出售7,000亿美元矿产，并为尼日利亚—美国委员会揭幕
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.body_zh:
阿布贾——固体矿产开发部长德勒·阿拉基博士驳斥了尼日利亚向美国出售价值7000亿美元固体矿产的报道，坚称尼日利亚与美国双边合作框架下没有出售或转让任何国家资产。阿拉基周二在阿布贾为尼日利亚—美国固体矿产领域战略合作委员会揭幕时发表上述言论。他称这些报道是虚假消息，并澄清协议旨在吸引投资，促进美国投资者与尼日利亚运营商开展合作。他说：“没有任何尼日利亚资产被出售，也没有任何东西易手。”

部长解释道，尼日利亚与美国签署的谅解备忘录是一个政府间平台，旨在促进企业间商业接洽，而非将尼日利亚矿产资源的所有权转让给外国利益集团。他说：“我们搭建了一个平台，让美国投资业务与尼日利亚本地运营商携手合作。协议已向公众公开，我们公开签署，并刊登在四五家全国性报纸上。”

该委员会的揭幕仪式是在两国于纽约举行的第81届联合国大会期间确立战略合作框架后举行的。阿拉基还驳斥了美国意图接管尼日利亚矿产资源和安全架构的说法，称这些报道具有误导性。他说，合作符合博拉·蒂努布总统的经济多元化议程，即通过可持续开发矿产资源，减少尼日利亚对原油的依赖。

据他介绍，尼日利亚正寻求改变国际经济交易模式。在这一模式下，非洲资源丰富国家出口原材料，却未能从资源开发中保留足够的价值。他说：“我们拥有资源，也拥有世界转向清洁能源所需的关键元素。因此，我们正在创立一种新范式——你们带来资本、专业知识和技术，与我们的自然资源相结合，创造双赢局面。投资者获得收益，尼日利亚也获得收益。”

部长惋惜地表示，尼日利亚长期以来实行单一产品经济模式，而其固体矿产行业很大程度上仍处于非正规状态，矿石通常“从矿坑运往港口”，缺乏充分的本地加工。他说，联邦政府出台了一项政策，将本地加工设为授予矿业权的前提条件，投资者必须证明其在国内加工矿产的明确路径。据阿拉基称，这项政策鼓励了全国范围内加工设施的建设，其中包括他所说的西非最大锂加工厂，该厂最近已由副总统在纳萨拉瓦州主持投产。

他说，政府的改革努力也为非洲矿产战略小组的成立提供了指导，该小组旨在加强非洲各国在矿产开发方面的合作。阿拉基将投资者信心回升归因于蒂努布政府实施的宏观经济改革，并称这些改革就土地使用权的保障以及利润汇回提供了保证。

部长要求新揭幕的委员会成员勤勉履职，并表示委员会肩负的使命对于实现总统提出的经济规模达到1万亿美元的目标至关重要。他敦促委员会协调各项活动、发掘可行的投资机会，并将尼日利亚—美国合作框架转化为可衡量的成果，从而巩固尼日利亚在全球固体矿产产业中的地位。

在欢迎辞中，固体矿产开发部常务秘书法鲁克·优素福·亚博工程师表示，此次揭幕将把日益增多的双边接触转化为务实合作和投资动员的结构化框架。美国大使馆经济官员乔纳森·巴斯也出席并发言，称美国总统唐纳德·特朗普已要求美国大使馆优先关注三个领域：能源、人工智能与超级智能，以及关键矿产。巴斯说，华盛顿正在寻求能够保障关键矿产供应链的合作伙伴关系，同时确保伙伴国家能够分享所创造的价值。

他说：“我们今天刚在尼日利亚经济峰会上签署了一份合同，研究在尼日利亚建设人工智能数据中心的可行性。这就是华盛顿希望我们前进的方向。”

尼日利亚固体矿产公司首席执行官兼董事总经理在致谢辞中表示，该委员会将协调合作框架的落实，促进投资，并监督实现尼日利亚—美国合作框架目标的进展。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.body: Telecel Ghana marked World Sustainability Day with a renewed commitment to practical climate action, showcasing how it integrates sustainability into its network operations, products, employee culture, and social impact initiatives. The organisation celebrated this year’s World Sustainability Day as a premium partner of the Ghana National Climate & ESG Policy Summit 2026, organised by Intelligence Nature International under the auspices of the Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability. The summit brought together policymakers, regulators, development institutions, and private-sector leaders to discuss Ghana’s green transition and businesses' role in accelerating climate action. Speaking during a private-sector panel discussion, Rita Agyeiwaa Rockson, Head of Sustainability, Foundation and External Communications at Telecel Ghana, called for sustainability to move from complex concepts and high-level commitments to practical actions organisations, entrepreneurs, and individuals can understand and adopt. “Sustainability cannot remain a conversation that only happens at the top, based on the assumption that everyone understands it. We need to simplify the language and connect it to the everyday decisions of organisations and individuals. When people understand how sustainability reduces costs, strengthens resilience and improves access to customers and investors, it becomes relevant to them,” Rita said. She encouraged organisations to start with achievable interventions, measure results, and use credible data to build toward broader climate ambitions. “There are practical actions that corporate organisations, small businesses and individuals can take to contribute to the larger sustainability goals we want to achieve. The important thing is to start, collect the data and communicate the impact being created,” she added. For Telecel Ghana, this approach is reflected in how the organisation integrates sustainability across its operations. To reduce the environmental footprint of its operations, Telecel Ghana is transitioning parts of its network infrastructure to renewable energy, with 15 exchanges currently powered by solar. The investment reduces its reliance on the national grid and supports more sustainable network operations. In August 2026, Telecel Ghana introduced its biodegradable Eco-SIM, manufactured with 90 per cent less plastic than standard SIM cards. The organisation has also planted more than 40,000 trees across the Achimota, Chipa and South Fomangso forest reserves, contributing to reforestation and ecosystem restoration. Its sustainability efforts also extend to digital and financial inclusion. Telecel Ghana’s services let customers complete essential transactions remotely, reducing the need to travel, costs, and associated emissions. Its digital inclusion initiatives equip entrepreneurs, including women-led businesses, with the skills and tools to improve efficiency, access new markets and strengthen their enterprises. According to Rita, inclusion must remain central to Ghana’s transition to a greener economy. “As we build the communities and economies of the future, we must pay attention to who is being included. Digital and financial inclusion are essential to ensuring that the benefits of sustainable development reach entrepreneurs, small businesses and underserved communities,” she said. Throughout the Month, Telecel Ghana also encouraged employees to make more environmentally responsible choices. Activities included No-Plastic Days, which promoted alternatives to single-use plastics, and a Green Market that connected employees with local entrepreneurs offering environmentally responsible and locally made products. The activities demonstrated how everyday choices can promote responsible consumption while creating opportunities for entrepreneurs advancing circular production. The organization’s participation in the summit extended the internal campaign into a broader national conversation on climate action, sustainable finance, ESG disclosure, carbon markets and green investment. “We recognise that sustainability is a journey and that there is still more work to be done. Our ambition is clear: connect people and organisations in ways that support a more inclusive society while progressively reducing our environmental impact. Achieving this requires collaboration across sectors, practical action and consistent measurement of progress,” Rita said. Telecel Ghana’s sustainability agenda rests on four pillars: Responsible Business, Inclusion for All, Environmental Responsibility, and Sustainable Society. These pillars guide how the organisation manages its operations, deploys technology, supports communities and contributes to Ghana’s sustainable development. Through investments in renewable energy, responsible products, environmental restoration, digital inclusion and employee engagement, Telecel Ghana is working to make sustainability an enduring part of its business and the communities it serves
https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.title_zh: Telecel Ghana在全国ESG峰会上展示务实的气候行动
https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.body_zh:
加纳Telecel以实际行动强化承诺纪念世界可持续发展日，并展示如何将可持续发展融入网络运营、产品、员工文化和社会影响项目。该公司以高级合作伙伴身份参加2026年加纳国家气候与ESG政策峰会，庆祝今年的世界可持续发展日。峰会由Intelligence Nature International组织，在气候变化与可持续发展国务部长办公室支持下举行。峰会汇聚政策制定者、监管机构、发展机构和私营部门领袖，讨论加纳的绿色转型以及企业在加快气候行动方面的作用。

Telecel加纳可持续发展、基金会与对外传播负责人Rita Agyeiwaa Rockson在私营部门专题讨论中呼吁，可持续发展不应只停留在复杂理念和高层承诺上，而应转化为组织、创业者和个人都能理解并采取的实际行动。

Rita表示：“可持续发展不能只是一场只在高层进行的对话，更不能建立在所有人都理解它的假设之上。我们需要简化相关表述，并将其与组织和个人的日常决策联系起来。当人们明白可持续发展如何降低成本、增强韧性以及改善接触客户和投资者的渠道时，它才会真正与他们产生关联。”

她鼓励各组织从可实现的干预措施入手，衡量结果，并利用可信数据推动更宏大的气候目标。Rita补充道：“企业组织、小型企业和个人都可以采取实际行动，为实现我们期望的更大可持续发展目标作出贡献。重要的是迈出第一步、收集数据，并传达由此产生的影响。”

对Telecel加纳而言，这一方针体现在该公司将可持续发展融入各项运营的方式中。为减少运营对环境造成的影响，Telecel加纳正将部分网络基础设施转换为可再生能源，目前已有15个交换局由太阳能供电。这项投资减少了公司对国家电网的依赖，并支持更加可持续的网络运营。

2026年8月，Telecel加纳推出可生物降解的Eco-SIM，其制造过程使用的塑料比标准SIM卡少90%。该组织还在Achimota、Chipa和South Fomangso森林保护地种植了4万多棵树，为再造林和生态系统恢复作出贡献。

其可持续发展工作还延伸至数字普惠和金融普惠。Telecel加纳的服务让客户能够远程完成必要交易，从而减少出行需求、成本及相关排放。其数字普惠项目为创业者，包括女性创办的企业，提供技能和工具，帮助他们提高效率、开拓新市场并增强企业实力。

Rita表示，包容必须继续成为加纳向更绿色经济转型的核心。“在建设未来的社区和经济时，我们必须关注谁正被纳入其中。数字普惠和金融普惠对于确保可持续发展的成果惠及创业者、小型企业和服务不足的社区至关重要。”

在整个活动月期间，Telecel加纳还鼓励员工作出更具环境责任的选择。相关活动包括提倡减少一次性塑料制品的‘无塑料日’，以及把员工与提供环保及本地制造产品的当地创业者连接起来的绿色市场。这些活动表明，日常选择既可以促进负责任消费，也能为推动循环生产的企业创造机会。

该公司参加峰会，将内部活动扩展至围绕气候行动、可持续金融、ESG披露、碳市场和绿色投资的更广泛全国讨论。Rita表示：“我们认识到，可持续发展是一段旅程，仍有更多工作要做。我们的目标十分明确：以支持更具包容性的社会的方式连接人们和组织，同时逐步减少我们的环境影响。实现这一目标需要跨部门协作、实际行动以及持续衡量进展。”

Telecel加纳的可持续发展议程建立在四大支柱之上：负责任业务、人人包容、环境责任和可持续社会。这些支柱指引该组织管理运营、部署技术支持社区并为加纳的可持续发展作出贡献。

通过投资可再生能源、负责任的产品、环境恢复、数字普惠和员工参与，Telecel加纳正努力让可持续发展成为其业务及其所服务社区的一项长期特征

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.summary: “There are circumstances on their side, so I think we need to hear what they have to say,” Kang told reporters when asked whether the meeting could be pushed beyond December. However, the U.S. Department of Defense said Tuesday that the meeting was expected to be held in early 2027, citing scheduling conflicts among senior officials. The agreement reached on Wednesday confirmed the postponement, ending uncertainty over whether the annual meeting would take place this year.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.summary_zh: “他们那边存在一些情况，因此我认为我们需要听听他们的说法。”当记者问及会议能否推迟至12月以后时，康这样表示。不过，美国国防部周二称，预计会议将于2027年初举行，理由是高级官员之间存在日程冲突。周三达成的协议确认了此次延期，从而结束了这场年度会议是否会于今年举行的不确定性。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body: Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul and U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed the postponement during their first face-to-face meeting Wednesday on the sidelines of a regional defense gathering in Cebu, Philippines. The two also agreed to hold a bilateral defense meeting in Washington in December, ahead of the rescheduled SCM, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening defense cooperation and maintaining a strong combined defense posture. The meeting, initially scheduled to take 15 minutes, lasted about 40 minutes. Conducted with simultaneous interpretation, the extended talks allowed for in-depth discussion of alliance issues. Before departing for the Philippines, Kang said the SCM schedule might need to be discussed with Washington, noting that the U.S. side had its own situation to consider. “There are circumstances on their side, so I think we need to hear what they have to say,” Kang told reporters when asked whether the meeting could be pushed beyond December. Asked whether he would personally raise the SCM schedule with Hegseth, Kang said, “I think we need to discuss it if necessary. I believe it is an important issue.” The SCM is traditionally held in the fall. However, the U.S. Department of Defense said Tuesday that the meeting was expected to be held in early 2027, citing scheduling conflicts among senior officials. The agreement reached on Wednesday confirmed the postponement, ending uncertainty over whether the annual meeting would take place this year. Kang and Hegseth also agreed that holding a successful 58th SCM would be important for the alliance. Before the agreement, a U.S. defense official had described the decision to postpone the meeting as having been mutually agreed upon, but Seoul maintained that no schedule had been finalized. Earlier Wednesday, Korea’s defense ministry had said, “We are consulting with the U.S. Department of Defense, taking into account mutually available dates, and no specific details have been finalized.” Despite the differing public statements, scheduling difficulties on the U.S. side are believed to be a major factor behind the delay. Washington faces competing priorities, including ongoing military operations and political developments at home, which could complicate efforts to arrange the annual meeting before the end of the year. “As the minister has repeatedly said, there are no major differences between Korea and the U.S.,” a military official noted. “Any differences at the military level can be resolved through close consultations.” Hegseth expressed hope that the two countries would strengthen defense cooperation while maintaining a robust combined defense posture. While the allies have faced questions over the pace of OPCON transfer, the latest talks indicated that both sides remain committed to moving the process forward through close consultations. The postponement comes as Seoul seeks to complete the full operational capability (FOC) verification of the future Combined Forces Command and agree with Washington on a target year for OPCON transfer. Kang told lawmakers Monday that the government was working with the United States to complete the verification process and determine a target year by the end of 2026. FOC verification is the second stage of a three-stage, conditions-based process to assess the readiness of a future combined command led by a Korean four-star general. The allies have also faced questions over whether the standards used to assess the conditions for OPCON transfer should change to reflect evolving security threats. The FOC verification is also understood to assess specific capabilities required for the future combined command to carry out its missions, rather than the overall military capabilities of the alliance, which continue to evolve in response to changing security threats
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.title_zh: 韩美年度安全会议推迟至2027年初举行
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/.body_zh: 国防部长姜信哲与美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞思周三在菲律宾宿务举行的一场地区防务会议期间首次面对面会晤时，确认了会议延期。两人还同意于12月在华盛顿举行双边防务会议，时间早于重新安排的SCM，并重申加强防务合作、维持强大联合防务态势的承诺。这次会议原定持续15分钟，最终约谈了40分钟。会谈采用同声传译进行，双方得以深入讨论联盟问题。启程前往菲律宾前，姜信哲表示，可能需要与华盛顿讨论SCM的日程安排，并指出美方也有自身情况需要考虑。当记者问及会议是否会推迟至12月之后时，姜信哲对记者说：“他们那边存在一些情况，因此我认为我们需要听听他们的意见。”当被问及是否会亲自与赫格塞思讨论SCM日程时，姜信哲说：“我认为如有必要，我们需要就此进行讨论。我相信这是一个重要问题。”SCM传统上于秋季举行。然而，美国国防部周二表示，预计会议将于2027年初举行，理由是高级官员的日程安排存在冲突。周三达成的协议确认了延期，结束了今年是否举行年度会议的不确定性。姜信哲和赫格塞思还认为，成功举行第58届SCM对联盟至关重要。在达成协议前，一名美国国防官员曾将推迟会议的决定描述为双方共同商定的结果，但首尔方面坚持称尚未敲定日程。周三早些时候，韩国国防部表示：“我们正与美国国防部进行磋商，考虑双方可行的日期，具体安排尚未敲定。”尽管双方公开表态不一，但据认为，美方日程安排困难是此次推迟的主要原因。华盛顿面临多项优先事项，包括仍在进行的军事行动和国内政治局势，这可能使在年底前安排年度会议变得复杂。一名军方官员指出：“正如部长多次所说，韩国与美国之间没有重大分歧。”“军方的任何分歧都可以通过密切磋商解决。”赫格塞思表示，希望两国在维持强大联合防务态势的同时加强防务合作。尽管盟国在战时作战指挥权移交的进度问题上受到质疑，但最新会谈显示，双方仍致力于通过密切磋商推动该进程。正值首尔寻求完成未来联合司令部全面作战能力验证，并与华盛顿就战时作战指挥权移交的目标年份达成一致之际，会议宣布延期。姜信哲周一对议员表示，政府正与美国合作完成验证流程，并在2026年底前确定目标年份。全面作战能力验证是基于条件、分三个阶段进行的进程中的第二阶段，用于评估由一名韩国四星上将指挥的未来联合司令部的战备状态。盟国还面临一些问题，即用于评估战时作战指挥权移交条件的标准是否应作出改变，以反映不断演变的安全威胁。全面作战能力验证据理解还将评估未来联合司令部履行任务所需的具体能力，而非联盟整体军事能力；后者仍在随着安全威胁的变化而不断演进

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.summary_zh: 韩国大型烘焙企业Sangmidang Holdings副董事长Hur Jin-soo本周早些时候在巴黎会见了Gellert Global Group（GGG）董事长George Gellert以及美国驻法国大使Charles Kushner，以探讨在海外市场建立更广泛合作伙伴关系。访问巴黎期间，Hur还会见了欧洲食品配料供应商和烘焙制造商，探讨能够支持Samlip和Paris Baguette拓展欧洲市场的合作方案。Paris Baguette是Sangmidang旗下全球化烘焙咖啡馆连锁品牌。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.body: Hur Jin-soo, vice chairman of Korean bakery giant Sangmidang Holdings, met Gellert Global Group (GGG) Chairman George Gellert and U.S. Ambassador to France Charles Kushner in Paris earlier this week to explore broader partnerships in overseas markets. Sangmidang said Wednesday that Hur discussed business developments and potential cooperation with Gellert and other GGG executives. Samlip, Sangmidang’s mass-market bakery subsidiary, could work with GGG to expand through U.S. supermarket and food service distribution networks and potentially enter Canada and Mexico, the Korean company said. U.S.-based GGG imports and distributes food products to retailers, food service distributors, restaurants, hotels, cruise operators and food manufacturers across North America. It sources more than 4,000 products from 60 countries and generates more than $1.7 billion in sales per year. The discussion first took place on Oct. 18 when Hur attended a reception for GGG’s partner firms at the U.S. ambassador’s residence in Paris. Hosted by Kushner, the event brought together about 130 representatives from 80 companies. Sangmidang said it was the only Korean company invited. The following day, Gellert and Kushner visited Samlip’s booth at SIAL Paris 2026, a major international food products exhibition across Europe. During his visit to Paris, Hur also met with European food ingredient suppliers and bakery manufacturers to explore partnerships that could support the European expansion of Samlip and Paris Baguette, Sangmidang’s global bakery café franchise. The company described the meetings as groundwork for broader cooperation. “The invitation to the U.S. ambassador’s residence in France was a meaningful occasion to further strengthen trust with global partners and build networks for expansion in North America and Europe,” a Sangmidang Holdings official said
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.title_zh: Sangmidang通过全球合作伙伴关系寻求拓展北美和欧洲市场
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.body_zh: 韩国烘焙业巨头Sangmidang Holdings副董事长Hur Jin-soo本周早些时候在巴黎会见了Gellert Global Group（GGG）董事长George Gellert和美国驻法国大使Charles Kushner，以探讨在海外市场建立更广泛合作伙伴关系。Sangmidang周三表示，Hur与Gellert及GGG其他高管讨论了业务发展和潜在合作事宜。Sangmidang旗下面向大众市场的烘焙子公司Samlip可与GGG合作，通过美国超市和餐饮服务分销网络扩大业务，并有望进入加拿大和墨西哥市场。韩国公司表示，总部位于美国的GGG向北美各地的零售商、餐饮服务分销商、餐厅、酒店、邮轮运营商和食品制造商进口并分销食品产品。公司从60个国家采购4,000多种产品，每年销售额超过$1.7 billion。双方于10月18日首次举行讨论，当时Hur出席了在巴黎美国大使官邸为GGG合作伙伴举行的招待会。招待会由Kushner主持，约有来自80家公司的130名代表参加。Sangmidang表示，它是唯一获邀出席的韩国公司。次日，Gellert和Kushner参观了Samlip在欧洲举办的大型国际食品产品展览会SIAL Paris 2026上的展位。Hur赴巴黎期间还会见了欧洲食品配料供应商和烘焙制造商，以探讨能够支持Samlip及Sangmidang旗下全球烘焙咖啡连锁品牌Paris Baguette拓展欧洲业务的合作项目。该公司称，这些会面为更广泛的合作奠定了基础。Sangmidang Holdings一名官员表示：“受邀前往法国美国大使官邸是一个加深与全球合作伙伴信任，并为拓展北美和欧洲业务建立合作网络的重要机会。”

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The House of Representatives Committee on Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education has given the management of Kaduna Polytechnic 72 hours to submit records of its internally generated revenue (IGR), pension deductions, National Housing Fund (NHF) contributions and other financial transactions. The directive followed concerns raised by the committee over the institution’s declining revenue despite an increase in its student population, as well as the need to verify the remittance of statutory deductions and payment of benefits to families of deceased staff. The committee’s Chairman, Fuad Laguda (APC, Lagos), issued the directive on Tuesday during an oversight visit to the institution, asking the management to submit the outstanding documents to the National Assembly within three working days. The requested documents include the institution’s staff nominal roll, full-time and part-time student population, evidence of remittances for pension deductions, records of NHF contributions, and details of death benefits paid to the families of deceased employees between 2023 and 2025. The lawmakers also demanded information on the institution’s investments, corporations, procurement and maintenance activities, renovation works in the security division and the School of Health Technology, as well as a list of its external solicitors. Figures presented by the institution showed that its IGR fell from N1.478 billion in 2023 to N1.398 billion in 2024 and N1.332 billion in 2025. The figures prompted the committee to question the accuracy of the revenue records, particularly given the reported growth in student enrolment. Mr Laguda said the figures appeared lower than expected and asked the management to provide a comprehensive account of the institution’s revenue and expenditure. “Taking a rough calculation of what we are doing here, it looks as if what you have given us is under-declared. The figure is too low. In other words, it seems what you are giving us here is not accurate,” he said. The committee also sought clarification on approximately N1.3 billion in pension deductions, demanding documentary evidence that the money had been remitted to the appropriate authorities. Mr Laguda said the committee needed the records to establish whether the institution had met its statutory obligations. The lawmakers also questioned the handling of death benefits for former employees, noting that more than 30 staff members reportedly died between 2023 and 2025. Mr Laguda said the committee had not received evidence showing that the benefits had reached the deceased employees’ next of kin. “In terms of death benefits, over 30 staff died during these years (2023-2025), yet there is no evidence of the payments of the benefits to their next of kin. We would like to have a comprehensive breakdown of this,” he said. The committee then requested a detailed account of the benefits and how they were paid. During the inspection, the lawmakers also examined the institution’s facilities, including an upgraded studio for its Departments of Media and Mass Communication. Mr Laguda said the committee was not fully satisfied with the condition of some facilities, adding that it needed more documentation before it could reach a conclusion on the issues raised. He said the institution needed to improve the condition of its buildings and ensure that its available resources were properly utilised. “We’ve asked them to make further submissions to us at the National Assembly within 72 hours. That is three working days,” he said. Responding to the lawmakers’ concerns, the Rector of Kaduna Polytechnic, Suleiman Umar, said the institution had remitted all pension deductions and was up to date with its obligations. Mr Umar, who was represented by the Deputy Rector (Academic), Aliyu Usman, said the institution had no outstanding issues regarding pension remittances. “As for pension, we do not have any issues at all. All our pension deductions are promptly remitted. In fact, even though the October salary has not been paid, the pension has been raised,” he said. He also explained that the institution did not directly pay death benefits to the families of deceased employees, saying the payments were handled by the relevant insurance companies. On security expenditure, he said the institution outsourced its security services to private security organisations. Mr Umar further maintained that the institution had no outstanding issues concerning NHF deductions and that the relevant records were available for submission to the committee. He assured the lawmakers that the management would provide all requested documents within the stipulated 72-hour deadline. The committee is expected to review the submissions before determining whether the institution complied with its financial and statutory obligations
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title_zh: 众议员要求卡杜纳理工学院在72小时内解释收入下降及养老金扣款问题
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 众议院联邦理工学院与高等技术教育委员会已要求Kaduna Polytechnic管理层在72小时内提交其内部创收（IGR）、养老金扣款、国家住房基金（NHF）缴款及其他财务交易的记录。该指令源于委员会提出的担忧，尽管学生人数有所增加，该校收入却持续下降，同时还需核实法定扣款项是否上缴，以及是否向已故员工的家属支付福利。委员会主席Fuad Laguda（APC，拉各斯）周二在对该校进行监督访问时发出指令，要求管理层在3个工作日内将尚未提交的文件交给国民议会。要求提交的文件包括该校员工名册、全日制和非全日制学生人数、养老金扣款上缴凭证、NHF缴款记录，以及2023年至2025年向已故员工家属支付死亡福利的明细。议员还要求提供该校投资、企业、采购和维护活动、安保部门及Health Technology学院装修工程，以及外部律师事务所名单的相关信息。该校提交的数据显示，其IGR从2023年的N1.478 billion降至2024年的N1.398 billion，并在2025年进一步降至N1.332 billion。鉴于据报学生注册人数有所增长，这些数字促使委员会质疑收入记录的准确性。Laguda先生表示，相关数字低于预期，并要求管理层对该校收入和支出作出全面说明。他说：“根据我们目前工作的大致估算，你们交给我们的数据似乎存在少报。数字太低了。换句话说，你们在这里提交给我们的资料似乎并不准确。”委员会还要求澄清约N1.3 billion的养老金扣款，并要求提供文件证据，证明相关款项已上缴至主管机关。Laguda先生表示，委员会需要这些记录，以确定该校是否履行了法定义务。议员还质疑前员工死亡福利的处理情况，并指出据报2023年至2025年间有30多名员工去世。Laguda先生说，委员会尚未收到任何证据，显示相关福利已支付给已故员工的近亲属。他说：“在死亡福利方面，这些年间（2023-2025年）有30多名员工去世，但没有证据表明相关福利已支付给他们的近亲属。我们希望获得一份全面、详细的明细。”随后，委员会要求就相关福利及其支付方式作出详细说明。在检查过程中，议员还查看了该校的设施，包括为Media and Mass Communication系升级的演播室。Laguda先生说，委员会对部分设施的状况并不完全满意，并表示在就所提出的问题作出结论之前，需要获得更多文件。他说，该校需要改善建筑物状况，并确保现有资源得到妥善利用。他说：“我们已要求他们在72小时内，也就是3个工作日内，向我们在国民议会的团队作进一步提交。”针对议员的关切，Kaduna Polytechnic校长Suleiman Umar表示，该校已上缴全部养老金扣款，并已履行所有义务。由副校长（学术事务）Aliyu Usman代表出席的Umar先生说，该校养老金上缴不存在任何未完成的问题。他说：“养老金方面，我们完全没有问题。所有养老金扣款都已及时上缴。事实上，尽管10月份的工资尚未支付，但养老金已经发放。”他还解释说，该校并不直接向已故员工家属支付死亡福利，相关款项由有关保险公司处理。在安保支出方面，他说，该校已将安保服务外包给私营安保机构。Umar先生进一步强调，该校NHF扣款不存在任何未完成的问题，相关记录也可提交给委员会。他向议员保证，管理层将在规定的72小时期限内提交所有要求的文件。预计委员会将审核相关提交材料，再确定该校是否遵守了财务和法定义务

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/reps.summary: The House of Representatives has approved a ₦100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for constructing the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/reps.summary_zh: 众议院已批准一项1005亿奈拉本票计划，用于向约贝州政府偿付在达马图鲁修建穆罕马杜·布哈里国际机场的费用。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/reps.body: The House of Representatives has approved a ₦100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for constructing the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu. The approved amount is ₦100,509,017,234.55, following the Federal Government’s decision to take over the newly constructed airport. The approval followed consideration of a report by the House Committee on Aids, Loans and Debt Management on Wednesday. Chairman of the committee, Abubakar Hassan Nalaraba, said during a briefing with journalists at the National Assembly, Abuja, that the committee conducted due diligence and inspected the facility before recommending the reimbursement. He said officials of the Federal Ministries of Aviation and Finance, alongside other relevant agencies, provided technical assessments and documentation on the project. “After due diligence and considerations, and after undertaking comprehensive oversight of the airport, receiving the reports of technical officials at the Ministry of Aviation, Ministry of Finance and the accounting office, we recently considered and approved the reimbursement of the airport to Yobe State Government,” Nalaraba said. He added that the committee found the quality of the airport’s infrastructure and equipment satisfactory, noting that professionals had certified the facilities as meeting the required standards. The committee’s report stated that the Federal Ministry of Aviation inspected the completed airport and confirmed that the quality of work met the standards required for its takeover by the Federal Government. It also found that the Yobe State Government had paid the contractors who executed the project, while the Bureau of Public Procurement certified that due process was followed. According to the report, the committee examined submissions from the state government, the Federal Ministries of Finance and Aviation, the Federal Executive Council and the Bureau of Public Procurement. It also reviewed contract agreements, certificates of completion, evidence of payments to contractors, due-process reviews and the bureau’s certificate of no objection. President Bola Tinubu had requested the National Assembly’s approval for the promissory note programme in a communication read on the floor of the House on October 13, 2026. The request was made pursuant to the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act, 2003, and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which provide for legislative approval of the programme. Promissory note programmes are used to settle outstanding Federal Government liabilities, including reimbursements to state governments for projects executed on behalf of the Federal Government. Speaking on the airport’s economic significance, Nalaraba said the facility would add value to residents of Yobe State and create opportunities for investment. “When you see a critical infrastructure being constructed in a state, I think it’s a value addition, first, to the people of the state. Secondly, it will attract some level of investment to the state and the nation at large,” he said. A member of the committee representing Yobe State, Mohammed Jajere, said the airport could serve as a cargo hub for the North-East, particularly for transporting agricultural produce and raw materials. “Yobe, as you all know, is an agrarian state. We are into agriculture and a lot of raw materials are abundantly available in the state, where we expect that the cargo airport will be used as a hub, especially in the North-East region, where you have these cargo airports,” he said. He added that the facility could help transport agricultural products from the region to other markets. However, journalists raised concerns about the commercial viability of airports in Nigeria, citing a report attributed to the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria indicating that only three of the country’s 22 domestic and international airports were commercially viable. In response, Nalaraba said the committee relied on assessments by the relevant aviation authorities, stressing that lawmakers were not technical specialists in airport operations. “The Ministry of Aviation, FAAN, in my earlier statement, I said technical FAAN has all gone and satisfied that this airport is viable and is ready for commercial use,” he said. He maintained that the project had undergone the necessary administrative and technical reviews before being presented to the National Assembly. The committee chairman also clarified that the reimbursement was not fresh funding for construction but repayment to Yobe State for money already spent on a project the Federal Government had decided to take over. “This is reimbursement. This money has been spent. The Federal and state governments spent this money to construct that cargo international airport,” he said. He added that the state government undertook the project despite aviation falling within the Federal Government’s exclusive legislative jurisdiction. On safeguards against additional financial liabilities, the committee said the Federal Government’s takeover meant responsibility for the airport, including its future maintenance and development, would rest with the federal authorities. The committee further indicated that the reimbursement would be a one-off payment, although detailed repayment arrangements were not fully explained during the briefing. The approval places the focus on the Federal Government’s management of the airport and whether the facility can attract sufficient commercial activity, particularly through agricultural cargo operations, to justify the public investment. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/reps.title_zh: 众议员批准为约贝州机场拨付1005亿奈拉偿还款
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/reps.body_zh: 众议院已批准一项₦1005亿本票计划，用于偿还约贝州政府为在达马图鲁建设穆罕马杜·布希里国际机场而垫付的资金。获批金额为₦100,509,017,234.55。此前，联邦政府决定接管这座新建机场。众议院于周三审议众议院援助、贷款和债务管理委员会提交的报告后批准了此项拨款。该委员会主席阿布巴卡尔·哈桑·纳拉拉巴在阿布贾国民议会接受记者简报时表示，委员会在建议偿还相关款项前进行了尽职调查，并实地检查了机场设施。他说，联邦航空部、财政部及其他相关机构的官员就该项目提供了技术评估和文件资料。纳拉拉巴说：“经过尽职调查和深入考虑，并对机场进行全面监督，同时收到航空部、财政部和会计办公室技术官员提交的报告后，我们最近审议并批准将机场偿还给约贝州政府。”他补充说，委员会认为机场基础设施和设备的质量令人满意，并指出专业人员已认证这些设施符合规定标准。委员会报告称，联邦航空部检查了已建成的机场，并确认工程质量符合联邦政府接管所需的标准。报告还发现，约贝州政府已向负责施工的承包商付款，而公共采购局则认证相关程序均已依法执行。据报告称，委员会审查了州政府、联邦财政部、联邦航空部、联邦执行委员会和公共采购局提交的材料。委员会还审阅了合同协议、竣工证明、向承包商付款的凭证、法定程序审查结果，以及公共采购局出具的无异议证明。2026年10月13日，博拉·蒂努布总统在众议院宣读的一份函件中，请求国民议会批准该本票计划。该请求依据《2003年债务管理办公室（设立）法》和《2007年财政责任法》提出，这两部法律均规定该计划须经立法机构批准。本票计划用于清偿联邦政府尚未偿付的债务，包括向代联邦政府实施项目的州政府偿还资金。谈及机场的经济意义时，纳拉拉巴表示，该设施将为约贝州居民增添价值，并创造投资机会。他说：“当您看到一座州内正在建设的重要基础设施时，我认为，首先它会为该州人民带来增值。其次，它会为该州乃至整个国家吸引一定程度的投资。”代表约贝州的委员会委员穆罕默德·贾杰雷表示，这座机场可以成为东北部地区的货运枢纽，尤其可用于运输农产品和原材料。他说：“各位都知道，约贝是一个农业州。我们从事农业，该州拥有大量原材料。我们期待这座货运机场能够作为枢纽使用，尤其是在东北部地区，因为当地拥有这些货运机场。”他补充说，该设施有助于将本地区的农产品运往其他市场。然而，记者对尼日利亚机场的商业可行性提出担忧，并援引一份据称出自尼日利亚联邦机场管理局的报告，称全国22座国内和国际机场中只有3座具备商业可行性。对此，纳拉拉巴表示，委员会依据相关航空主管部门的评估作出决定，并强调议员并非机场运营方面的技术专家。他说：“在我之前的声明中，我提到航空部、FAAN的技术人员已经全部完成检查，并确认这座机场具备商业可行性，已准备好投入商业运营。”他坚持认为，该项目在提交国民议会之前，已经完成必要的行政和技术审查。委员会主席还澄清，这笔偿还款并非用于建设的新资金，而是联邦政府决定接管项目后，向约贝州偿还其已经投入的资金。他说：“这是偿还款。这笔钱已经花出去了。联邦政府和州政府共同出资建设了这座国际货运机场。”他补充说，尽管航空事务属于联邦政府专属立法管辖范围，但州政府仍承担并推进了该项目。关于防止增加财政负担的保障措施，委员会表示，联邦政府接管后，机场的职责，包括未来的维护和发展，将由联邦主管部门承担。委员会进一步指出，这笔偿还款将一次性支付，尽管在简报期间并未对具体偿还安排作出充分说明。这项批准使人们将关注重点放在联邦政府对机场的管理，以及该设施能否通过吸引足够的商业活动，尤其是通过农产品货运业务，来证明公共投资的合理性。此处表达的意见不代表《Vanguard》报或该报任何员工的观点

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/nnpc.body: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) has pledged to resume oil exploration activities in Borno State, while assuring the state government of steps to address delays in upgrading the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant. The commitments were made on Wednesday when Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, received the NNPCL management team, led by the board chairman, Engr. Ahmadu Musa Kida, in Maiduguri. The meeting focused on energy development, the resumption of oil exploration in the state and the delayed completion of the emergency power plant upgrade. Zulum stressed the strategic importance of resuming exploration in the Borno Basin, noting that the state had considerable commercial potential and shared borders with three countries. He expressed optimism that renewed exploration efforts by the national oil company would help unlock the state’s hydrocarbon resources and stimulate economic development. The governor, however, expressed concern over the slow pace of work on the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant, describing the facility as critical to improving electricity supply in the state. He said the materials required for the plant’s upgrade had been on site for about two years, yet the project remained incomplete. Zulum urged the NNPCL management to intervene and remove the bottlenecks delaying the project, stressing that its completion was important to the socio-economic well-being of residents of Maiduguri and neighbouring communities. Responding, Kida assured the governor of the company’s readiness to fast-track the resumption of exploration activities in the Borno Basin and address the challenges delaying the power plant upgrade. He also commended Zulum for his continued support and efforts to create a conducive environment for investment in the state. The meeting was attended by the Deputy Governor, Umar Usman Kadafur; Secretary to the State Government, Bukar Tijani; Acting Chief of Staff, Dr. Babagana Mallumbe; and other senior government officials. Members of the NNPCL delegation included the Executive Vice President, Upstream, Mr. Udy Ntia, and the Executive Vice President, Gas, Power and New Energy, Mr. Olalekon Ogunleye.
